items.prompt: In sorted pair sum, the current left+right sum is below target. Why can left advance?

options.text: Every remaining partner at or before right is no larger
options.why: Using this same left with any remaining partner still gives too small a sum.

options.text: The left value must be exactly zero
options.why: The proof does not require zero or nonnegative values.

options.text: Every future input is already known to be a duplicate
options.why: The sorted-order argument does not depend on duplicates.

options.text: Moving either pointer arbitrarily always preserves solutions

items.explanation: Sortedness justifies discarding the too-small left value. Without it, the same move can discard a valid pair.
